newsitem.title: CANADA: Federated Pipe files gas liquids pipeline plan.
newsitem.headline: Federated Pipe files gas liquids pipeline plan.

text.p: Federated Pipe Lines (Northern) Ltd said on Thursday it filed an application with Canada's National Energy Board to build a 172 km (107-mile) gas liquids pipeline to Belloy, Alberta from Taylor, British Columbia.

Federated, co-owned by Anderson Exploration Ltd and Imperial Oil Ltd, said the C$41-million Taylor Pipeline would allow northeast B.C. gas producers to ship their ethane, propane and butane to Fort Saskatchewan, Alberta's main petrochemical hub.

It said the line would operate in batch mode and receive ethane plus, propane plus, segregated condensate and crude oil at Taylor, as well as crude oil and condensate via a truck terminal in the Spirit River area.
The pipeline would also allow B.C. crude producers to ship their volumes to markets to the west coast or Edmonton, Federated said.
The Taylor Pipeline, which will compete with others in the area, is estimated to be in service by the first quarter of 1998. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
